evals.name: sample-app-from-scratch
evals.prompt: we're putting onlyoffice in front of our go service and before i wire it into the real product i want something i can click through and show the team on friday. a page that lists whatever files we have, opens any of them properly and also read-only, lets me drop one in from my laptop, make a fresh empty spreadsheet or text doc, rename, delete. people keep mailing us .doc files from 2009 so those need to open too. document server is in docker on localhost:8080 with the jwt thing switched on, secret's in DOCS_JWT_SECRET, files on disk is fine as long as it survives a restart. write the tests as you go please, i've been burned by a pile of untested generated code before.
evals.expected_output: A Go integration with the five endpoints - the embedding page, the callback receiver, download, upload and convert - plus the list/rename/delete routes the demo page needs, with the dashboard page and its list/rename/delete routes behind their own package or build tag so the backend - the embedding page included - still builds and serves without them. document.key is derived from the stored file's current revision (counter, mtime or content hash) and changes on every committed revision (status 2, conversion, replacement) but not on a status-6 force-save, persisted alongside the file so a restart doesn't resurrect an old key. documentType is mapped from the extension family, callbackUrl and user live under editorConfig, handlers under events, and the whole config object is signed server-side into a root token; user.id is an anonymized session id. The callback verifies the body token before fetching url, branches the full status table, downloads on 2 and 6, and answers exactly {"error": 0}. The convert route sends Accept: application/json with lowercase filetype/outputtype, a body token, async polling that re-sends the identical request under the same key until endConvert, and maps the negative error codes individually. Supported pairs come from a vendored ONLYOFFICE/document-formats copy, whose auto-convert action is what drives the legacy .doc path; the create-new blanks are real binaries vendored from ONLYOFFICE/document-templates. The editor page's goback button points at the file list and onRequestClose actually navigates there rather than leaving the visitor on a blank page. Tests cover each endpoint and each implemented callback status branch and are written against the contract rather than against the implementation.
assertions: all five endpoints exist - the embedding page, the callback receiver, download, upload and convert - since the backend is what a third-party integrates against and it is a five-endpoint surface whether or not the demo page calls all of them

the demo page and its list/rename/delete routes are separable from the backend - own package, module, build tag or flag - and the backend still compiles and serves its endpoints with the page fully absent, not merely unrouted

document.key changes whenever a new revision is committed - the final save (status 2), a conversion, an upload replacing the file - and the value is persisted with the file rather than derived from the filename or minted fresh per page load, since the service serves its cached revision for a key it has seen before and reusing one across a save is what corrupts history; a force-save (status 6) stores the bytes but keeps the key, since the session is still open
the key survives a restart as the same value the last save produced - an in-memory counter that resets to zero hands the document server a key it already has under different content

documentType is derived from the file's extension family - docx to word, xlsx to cell, pptx to slide, pdf to pdf - rather than hardcoded or passed the extension itself, which is not one of the four accepted values
callbackUrl and user sit inside editorConfig and the handlers inside events, not at the config root, where the editor ignores them without raising anything

editorConfig.user.id is an opaque identifier minted per visitor session or per simulated user, not an email address or real name and not derived from one - a hash of a typed name or email is reversible by dictionary and counts as the name
every token is signed on the server with HS256 and the secret appears in no file the browser downloads and in no response the page fetches
the root token signs the same config object that is handed to DocsAPI.DocEditor, not a hand-picked subset of its fields
the callback verifies the body token before anything is fetched from url, since verifying afterwards leaves the window in which an unsigned caller makes the server download whatever it names
the callback handles status 2 and 6 by downloading from url and persisting, and treats 6 as a snapshot with the session still open rather than as a close
the callback's success response is exactly {"error": 0} - any other body reads to the editing service as a failed delivery and it retries the same callback indefinitely
the convert request sends Accept: application/json, without which the service answers in XML and the failure surfaces as a decode error pointing nowhere near the cause
filetype and outputtype are lowercased and filetype, key, outputtype and url are all sent
the conversion request carries its token inside the JSON body, which is the vector that service reads

an async conversion is polled by re-sending the identical request under the same key until endConvert is true, rather than sleeping a fixed interval or minting a new key per attempt, which starts the job over

the response's error key is checked before fileUrl is read, and the negative codes are distinguished from one another - -7 (input error, the closest documented code for an illegal pair) reported distinctly from -8 (invalid token) rather than folded into a generic failure
which conversions are possible is read from a vendored ONLYOFFICE/document-formats copy (onlyoffice-docs-formats.json) rather than a list of extensions written into the source
the legacy .doc/.xls/.ppt path is driven by that table's auto-convert action - converted to the family's OOXML target before edit is offered - rather than by an extension allowlist someone typed out

the blank files behind create-new are real binaries vendored from ONLYOFFICE/document-templates, not zip bytes or empty files the generator produced, and any missing format is raised as a scope question rather than synthesized
the file list offers at least edit and view per file plus rename and delete, since a single hardcoded document is the bare snippet this sample was asked to be more than

editorConfig.customization.goback points at the file list page and onRequestClose actually navigates back there after destroyEditor(), rather than only closing the editor and leaving the visitor on a blank page - the demo has a dashboard to return to and the editor has to hand them back to it
nothing styles or reads the placeholder element after init - the sizing is on a wrapper around it - because init replaces that element with an iframe and everything set on it is dropped

there is a test for each of the five endpoints and one for every callback status value the handler acts on (1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, plus any default branch it adds), even where two statuses share a branch, not a representative subset

the tests assert the contract - the exact {"error": 0} body, the Accept header, the lowercase types, the key changing across a save - rather than restating what the implementation was just written to do
no test reaches into the editor's iframe DOM, which is origin-isolated from the host page and cannot be inspected from it

evals.name: production-ready-react-rust-docspace-demo
evals.prompt: Build a production-ready, full-fledged demo application showcasing every Document Server API surface based on the official API documentation. The architecture must feature a robust Rust backend and a React frontend styled entirely in ONLYOFFICE's own DocSpace design language - the real DocSpace look and components, not a generic redesign wearing DocSpace colors. The frontend must act as a single-page application requiring authentication before rendering the workspace; a DocSpace-styled sidebar navigation, file manager grid/rows, and dialogs must gate access to a document dashboard where the user can view, upload, drop, create, rename, and delete files. User accounts on the Rust backend must live in a concurrency-safe in-memory store. The logged-in session must map securely to the current user passed into the ONLYOFFICE editor configuration. The editor view must implement the full configuration matrix: editing, review, form-filling and embedded modes, the complete document.permissions object, historical version comparison, comment/chat events, and both Fast and Strict co-editing. The Rust backend must safely issue JWT tokens (HS256) meeting ONLYOFFICE Docs's strict validation, orchestrate historical file revisions with content hashes, manage file lock and force-save cycles through the Command Service, convert non-OOXML types through the Conversion API, and expose a complete, hardened webhook handler tracking every callback status code (1 through 7). The entire system must be containerized with a secure docker-compose orchestration: health checks, an Nginx reverse proxy managing CORS/security headers and the Document Server address split, persistent volumes so nothing is lost on restart, and isolated networks.
evals.expected_output: A fully functional multi-container docker-compose stack - React frontend, Rust backend, Nginx reverse proxy, and ONLYOFFICE Document Server - with JWT enforced globally via a secret shared between the backend and the Document Server through environment variables. The Rust backend structures its domain behind Ports & Adapters: traits for each port with Clone + Send + Sync + 'static bounds, async ports returning impl Future rather than depending on async-trait, generics preferred over dyn Trait except where real runtime polymorphism is needed, and a composition root that wires concrete adapters together. User/session state lives in a concurrency-safe in-memory structure. The callback handler verifies the token before fetching url, branches every status 1-7 explicitly, and answers exactly {"error": 0} for everything it handled. The Command Service (forcesave/info/drop/meta/version) and the Conversion API (lowercase fields, Accept: application/json, async polling under the same key, individually mapped negative error codes, support driven by the vendored format table) are both mounted as their own reachable routes, not buried as internal-only steps. Version history persists an incremented number, actor, snapshot, and content hash per revision, and wires both the onRequestHistory/refreshHistory list and the onRequestHistoryData/setHistoryData diff-open pair. The React frontend is built on ONLYOFFICE's own docspace-ui-kit-react - its real components (Tiles/Rows/Table, Selectors, ModalDialog, Toast) and its globalColors theme tokens, not a hand-rolled imitation - gates the dashboard behind a real login/register flow, and initializes DocsAPI.DocEditor with the full permissions matrix, mode switching, coEditing choice, and a user identity drawn from the live session, wired back to the file list via goback/onRequestClose.
assertions: the docker-compose.yml defines separate services for the React frontend, Rust backend, Nginx proxy, and ONLYOFFICE Document Server, with only the Nginx service publishing a port to the host and the rest reachable only inside the compose network
all JWT tokens are signed HS256 with a secret read from the environment and shared between the Rust backend and the Document Server via JWT_SECRET, never hardcoded as a fallback in source

the Rust backend's output ports are defined as traits (not concrete structs) under a ports/domain module, with Clone + Send + Sync + 'static bounds, and async port methods return impl Future<Output = ...> + Send rather than pulling in the async-trait crate

the composition root wires concrete adapters into a generic service parameterized over its port types rather than boxing every port behind Arc<dyn Trait> by default, reserving dynamic dispatch for a case that genuinely needs runtime-chosen implementations

user and session state lives in a concurrency-safe in-memory structure (e.g. Arc<RwLock<...>>, a Mutex-guarded map, or an equivalent concurrent map) rather than an unsynchronized global, since concurrent requests can touch the same session

the callback/webhook endpoint verifies the signed token against the sibling root fields before fetching anything from url, branches statuses 1 through 7 explicitly rather than a subset, and returns exactly {"error": 0} for every status it handled, including the ones it only logs

status 2 and 6 both download and persist the file, with 6 leaving the editing session open rather than tearing it down, and a genuine internal failure answers non-zero instead of a false {"error": 0} that would silently lose the save

the Command Service is exposed as its own reachable route supporting forcesave, info, drop, meta, and version, with each response error code (0/1/2/3/4/6) mapped to a distinct branch rather than a generic failure

the Conversion API request lowercases filetype and outputtype, sends the token inside the JSON body, and sets the Accept: application/json header, without which the service replies in XML and the failure looks unrelated to the real cause

an async conversion is polled by re-sending the identical request under the same key until endConvert is true, and the frontend shows progress as a state or elapsed time - not the response's percent, which is only ever 0 or 100, and not a synthetic animation

which conversions are offered comes from a vendored ONLYOFFICE/document-formats copy rather than a hand-typed list, and the response's error key is checked before fileUrl is read, with negative codes (e.g. -7 input error vs -8 invalid token) mapped to distinct causes

each persisted document revision records an incremented version number, the acting user, the snapshot/changesurl location, and a content hash of the saved bytes, computed at save/force-save time rather than lazily when the history panel opens

both onRequestHistory -> refreshHistory (populating the version list) and onRequestHistoryData -> setHistoryData (opening one version's diff) are wired as the distinct event/method pairs they are, not just onRequestHistory alone and not conflated with onRequestRestore

editorConfig specifies document.permissions covering at least edit, comment, download, print, and fillForms, and the frontend exposes a way to switch the editor's mode among edit, view, review, and fillForms that updates the initial config accordingly
editorConfig.coEditing.mode is set explicitly to fast or strict rather than left to the editor's default, surfaced as a real application choice rather than hardcoded arbitrarily

editorConfig.user maps to the currently authenticated session's own identity (an anonymized id and display name), not a static mock user, and the token signs the whole assembled config object rather than a hand-picked subset of its fields

the frontend is built on docspace-ui-kit-react's own components (its Tiles/Rows/Table for the file manager, its ModalDialog/Toast for dialogs and notifications) and its globalColors theme tokens for the DocSpace look, rather than a freehand recreation of DocSpace's colors and layout from memory

since docspace-ui-kit-react is currently AGPL-3.0-licensed (not MIT), the agent either asked the user to choose between taking it on directly (making this project AGPL-3.0 too, with real LICENSE/README disclosure of the network-source obligation) or porting its token values/design into freshly-licensed code, rather than silently defaulting to either path or asserting an MIT license the kit doesn't actually carry
editorConfig.customization.goback points at the file manager/dashboard and onRequestClose actually navigates back there after destroyEditor(), rather than leaving the visitor on a blank page
nothing styles or queries the DocsAPI.DocEditor placeholder element outside its one constructor call, since init replaces it with an iframe and a leftover rule on it does nothing

the Nginx layer sets a Content-Security-Policy naming the Document Server origin under frame-src/connect-src (including the wss:// form), rather than a default-src 'self' that would silently block the editor iframe or its co-editing socket

CORS on the Nginx layer or the backend validates the request origin against an explicit allowlist rather than reflecting whatever Origin header arrives, especially anywhere Allow-Credentials is also set

storage for uploaded/created files and the Document Server's own data directory are both bound to named volumes that survive a docker compose down/up cycle, not left as container-local, ephemeral state

login, registration, and session state are real - a session actually gates access to the dashboard and maps to editorConfig.user - rather than a username picker simulating different users with no actual authentication behind it
